title: Validity and unsatisfiability are incorrectly equated with provability of the opposite sentence.
details:
[Heule, *Logic and Mechanized Reasoning: Skolemization*](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~mheule/15311-s26/slides/Skolemization.pdf),
Spring 2026 course, slides 6–7 (PDF pages 7–8). Type: false equivalences.

The fourth item on each slide asks whether the negated counterpart is provable,
although the preceding item asks whether that same sentence is unsatisfiable.
For slide 6, take `A(x)` to be `x=x`: its universal closure is valid, while
`∃x ¬A(x)` is unsatisfiable and is not provable in a sound calculus. For slide 7,
use `A(x)` equal to `x≠x`: the original existential sentence is not valid, but
the opposite universal sentence is valid and provable.

**Repair and corpus disposition:** replace the fourth item by refutability of
the opposite sentence, or by provability of its negation. These adjacent
slides are not used by an entry. The inspected witness-function arguments on
slides 12–13 support [Skolemization](entries/skolemization/entry.html#expansion-theorem)
and are unaffected.
